newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Elf reduces cost of Nigerian gas project.
newsitem.headline: Elf reduces cost of Nigerian gas project.

text.p: Elf Petroleum Nigeria Limited has scaled down by 20 percent from an initial estimate of $500 million the cost of a gas project to l feed Nigeria's planned prestigious Liquified Natural Gas (LNG) plant, a senior company official said.

"The pre-project team has been able to reduce the cost of the Obite Gas Project by almost 20 percent," Francois Viaud, executive general manager, oil and gas at Elf Petroleum Ltd wrote in the company's quarterly magazine just released.

"Through the pooling together of various ideas from production people, architects, the gas commercial and reservoir guys, we have been able to reduce capital expenditures by $100 million." Viaud said.

The gas project located on Oil Mining Lease (OML) 58 in the southeastern Rivers State is owned by the Nigerian National Petroleum Corp/Elf joint venture and will produce 7.15 million cubic metres of gas per day.
It is expected to go on stream in July 1999, ahead of the scheduled take-off of the LNG plant in October of the same year.
But there is concern the target date of completion may not be met because of the poor funding of joint venture operations by the Nigerian government.
"The first challenge to the project is to secure the joint venture budget, any delay in funding would impact on our capability to complete the project on time," Viaud said.
Elf Nigeria pumps 130,000 barrels per day of crude oil.
